text:
maya: Noticing a lineup of 12 pending multi-GPU jobs in eu-west-1; cluster shows plenty of total GPUs but scheduler won't pack them. Suspect fragmentation + mixed GPU flavors. Anyone oncall?
linus: I'm here. Quick check: `kubectl get pods -o=custom-columns=NODE:.spec.nodeName,GPU:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests.nvidia.com/gpu` shows many 1-GPU pods scattered. Big jobs need 4-16 contiguous GPUs.
omar: I pulled scheduler logs: many `PredicateFailure: Pod didn't fit` messages with reasons 'Insufficient allocatable nvidia.com/gpu' even though sum free GPUs >= request. Looks like resources are split across nodes.
tara: Can we use preemption to evict low-priority pods and consolidate? Last time we disabled preemption for serving; but maybe we can limit to `batch` namespace.
maya: Preemption globally off for customer-facing namespaces. We could enable it only for `batch/*` and `batch-high`. Need to be careful.
linus: Another lever: deploy a temporary descheduler policy to move 1-GPU batch pods together using `RemoveDuplicates` and `LowNodeUtilization`. That avoids killing serving pods.
jess: We also have a pool with mixed accelerators (A10 + T4). Some pods request `gpu-model: t4` which prevents them from moving. Mismatched labels are fragmentation source.
omar: Found 4 nodes with device-plugin flaps last 24h (node-9, node-31, node-78, node-79). When plugin restarted kubelet reported reduced allocatable, and some pods got stuck in `Terminating` with GPUs not freed.
autoscale-bot: [INFO] Cluster autoscaler: nodegroup-eu-gpu has 0/3 available spot capacity; on-demand quota left: 2 nodes.
linus: Quick plan options: (A) run descheduler for `batch` namespaces -> low disruption, moderate time; (B) taint a subset of nodes `reserved=big:NoSchedule` and drain 1-GPU pods to other pools -> immediate availability for big jobs; (C) temporarily enable selective preemption for non-serving pods; (D) request +1 on-demand large node as hotfix.
maya: Preference is minimal customer impact. Option A + D seems safe. Descheduler could take 20-40m; if not solved we spin up 1 large node.
tara: For descheduler, we should respect PodDisruptionBudgets. Add `--evict-local-storage=false` and only target pods with `scheduling=flexible` label.
jess: I'll run a `kubectl get pods -l scheduling=flexible -o wide` to estimate eviction count. Current estimate: ~18 pods across 12 nodes.
omar: Before evicting, I'll reconcile device-plugin state and force restart on nodes with restarts. That should free up a few GPUs without any pod moves.
linus: Also consider enabling `BinPacking` scoring weight up from 1 to 5 in scheduler policy so future pods pack tighter. But rolling that out requires careful testing.
maya: Action items: Omar restart GPU plugin on flagged nodes (ETA 15m). Jess gather flexible pods list (ETA 10m). Linus prepare descheduler manifest with PDB awareness and dry-run (ETA 30m). Tara file request for +1 large on-demand node in eu-west-1 (ETA 20m).
omar: Restarted plugin on node-9 and node-31; allocatable increased by 2 GPUs each. One 8-GPU job transitioned from Pending->Running for node-31. Continuing with node-78/79 now.
jess: Flexible pods list posted: 18 pods, namespaces batch, perf-tests. All have PDBs with minAvailable >=1 for 3 pods; we'll exclude those.
linus: Descheduler dry-run looks OK: would evict 12 pods respecting PDBs. If we approve, real run scheduled in 10m.
maya: Go ahead with descheduler real run only after Omar finishes plugin restarts. No evictions of serving namespaces.
autoscale-bot: [ALERT] 1759001700 - PendingLargeJobs - eu-west-1 - pending_multi_gpu=11
omar: Plugin restarts finished; node-78 had a stuck kubelet state, required machine reboot. That node is draining; ETA 12m.
linus: Descheduler run kicked off now (target label scheduling=flexible). Monitoring.
jess: Evictions progressing, 9 pods rescheduled, 3 remained due to PDB constraints. Big-job queue dropping.
maya: Monitoring SLA: p99 latency for online-serving unchanged. Nice.
tara: If fragmentation recurs, we should schedule an infra change: a dedicated `gpu-large` nodepool with label `size=large` and taint `reserved=big:NoSchedule` so batch/CI don't land there.
linus: Agree. Also propose a lifecycle job that periodically compacts GPUs (descheduler cron) during low-traffic hours.
maya: Good work. Postmortem items: device-plugin stability, mixed-label QoS causing fragmentation, and consider scheduler binpack weight. Closing once remaining 2 pending jobs start or we spin up fallback node.
autoscale-bot: [INFO] Runbook: https://intra.redwood/ops/gpu-packing-runbook
